newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech share indices fall as demand dries up.
newsitem.headline: Czech share indices fall as demand dries up.

text.p: The Czech PX50 and RPIX indices lost ground on Thursday with dealers seeing insufficient demand to sustain strong gains made at the end of last week and the beginning of this week.
The PX50 lost 0.5 percent to 556.9 while the major issue dominated RPIX fell 0.8 percent to 1,132.

Almost all the major issues fell on Thursday and dealers said they saw little chance of a rebound for several weeks citing nervousness about the health of the banking sector and political uncertainty ahead of the Senate elections in mid-November as the main causes of concern.
The one exception was Komercni Banka, dealers said, which rose 10 crowns to 2,318 making it the only gainer among the highly capitalised shares.
"Komercni is now benefiting from small depositers moving their deposits to bigger banks after the affair with Agrobanka and Kreditini Banka," said Lubomir Vystavel of ING Barings.
"Komercni's liquidity is also quite high," he said.

Many analysts have predicted a strengthening of the position of the big banks as some depositers move their accounts from smaller banks to what they perceive to be the relative safety of the country's most powerful financial institutions.
The central bank has so far had to intervene in the affairs of 12, mainly very small, banks.
Komercni is by far the biggest Czech bank in terms of capital and assets although savings bank Ceska Sporitelna has higher valued deposits.
